{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
# First, check for any remaining '999,999.99' or '999999.99' in string form
# We already found 6 rows with '999,999.99'

# Clean the revenue column
# Replace commas and convert to float
data['revenue_clean'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Now, filter out the six QA orders
qa_mask = data['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99
print(f"Number of QA orders after cleaning: {qa_mask.sum()}")

# Filter out QA orders and refunded orders
# Refunded orders should not be included in revenue or conversion metrics
# We are analyzing campaign success via conversion rate and revenue per order
filtered_data = data[~qa_mask & (data['status'] == 'completed')]

# Now, inspect the filtered data
print(f"Number of rows after filtering QA and refunded orders: {len(filtered_data)}")

# Check the distribution of channels and segments
print("\nChannel distribution:")
print(filtered_data['channel'].value_counts())

print("\nCustomer segment distribution:")
print(filtered_data['customer_segment'].value_counts())

# Check conversion rate by channel
conversion_by_channel = filtered_data.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean()
print("\nConversion rate by channel:")
print(conversion_by_channel)

# Check average revenue by channel
avg_revenue_by_channel = filtered_data.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].mean()
print("\nAverage revenue by channel:")
print(avg_revenue_by_channel)

# Cross-tabulate channel vs customer_segment to check for confounding
print("\nCross-tabulation: channel vs customer_segment")
print(pd.crosstab(filtered_data['channel'], filtered_data['customer_segment']))"}
